title: You’re Just a Youth Worker
origin: Every youth worker has heard some version of it. From a parent, a partner, a professional in a suit, sometimes from a colleague. Just a youth worker.
[KEYNOTE ORIGIN STORY — a short paragraph from Nahim on the specific moment or conversation that sparked this talk.]
about: This keynote takes that line apart. Nahim shows how the “just a youth worker” he was told he was became a catalyst for systemic change in one of the country’s most deprived boroughs, and makes the case that youth work is one of the most important leadership roles in society.
It’s personal, it’s direct, and it’s not just for youth workers. Anyone who has been underestimated, or who leads people who are, will recognise themselves in it.
takeaways: A different way of seeing the people at the bottom of your organisation chart
What trust actually looks like, and why it’s built in ordinary moments
How to lead from lived experience without being defined by it
Why “hard to reach” is a mirror, not a label
Practical ways to look after the people who look after everyone else
